sources.title: Amendments and Nonconformance Penalties for Model Year 2027 and Later Heavy-Duty Highway Engines and Vehicles (proposed)
EPA proposes cost-saving revision to 2027 truck emission rule

status_summary: On 2025-03-12 the EPA Administrator announced that EPA would reevaluate its 2023 heavy-duty nitrogen oxide final rule, according to the later proposal. On 2026-07-14 EPA published a proposed rule for model year 2027 and later heavy-duty engines that does not reopen the NOx, particulate, hydrocarbon and carbon monoxide standards but would keep model year 2026 warranty periods, delay the longer useful life periods to model year 2030, create nonconformance penalties for certain diesel engines, and replace engine power derates with visible or audible notifications for urea system inducements. EPA estimated warranty savings of up to 6,000 dollars per diesel vehicle. Comments closed 2026-08-29, and no final rule was found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-13.

timeline.event: The EPA Administrator announced that EPA would reevaluate the 2023 heavy-duty NOx final rule, as recounted in the 2026 proposal.
EPA announced the proposal, according to Transport Topics, with comments due 2026-08-29.
EPA published a proposed rule amending compliance provisions, warranty and useful life periods, nonconformance penalties and inducement rules for model year 2027 and later heavy-duty engines.

title: Reconsider the heavy-duty truck NOx rule to cut cost and compliance burden
